categories.queue-standing-note: Every queued intent record appears in the list above, newest first: a row is written the moment a button is clicked, so an empty list simply means nothing has been queued on this node yet.
categories.queued: Intent queued — the local worker applies it.
categories.remove-confirm-msg: Every post or draft referencing this category is migrated to the target category, then the category record itself is deleted by this node's worker — the category is never left dangling.

categories.worker-note: Buttons only queue the action; this node's worker performs it. The browser never rewrites a post.

diagnostics.adv-desc: Level-3 detail, folded here: storage & index, the log surface, data export / backup, the permission surface, the background intent queue and first-line troubleshooting. Every command is copy-and-run; nothing on this page executes. How to read them: run the storage audit bare — it answers through its exit code (0 = every layout is files and the index is fresh) and its JSON report grows past 64KB, so a piped fragment is not a report (arc-contracts §4.1a). arc space sync converges --to toward --from and --mirror DELETES destination-only files, so preview with --dry-run. The AFS records are the source of truth and dist/ is rebuildable, so keep an OFFLINE copy of node.key (content-signing key) and .env.local (chain configuration) outside this repo — they are not AFS records; losing them loses the node identity, and they must never be committed or written into AFS. DID Space: /user is a caller-scoped projection, not a directory — arc space list --scope user and arc space path --scope user address it (substitute the app DID), and the reading-list CLI addresses records by reader DID; this daemon has AFS_DID_SPACE_SCOPE_SECRET UNSET, so scope directories are plaintext (de-identification OFF) — a daemon environment variable ArcBlog can only register as a production prerequisite, never set. Permissions: this platform gives the app exactly two roles, guest and admin (blocklet.yaml replicated.readRole / minRole) — there is no finer grant to look for. Background work: a console chain button only writes an intent record; the node's own worker signs it on the chain (the signing key never reaches the browser) — that is the worker command above. No heartbeat record exists anywhere in this codebase, so an empty queue is a normal state, not an error, and there is no last-seen time to show.
diagnostics.cmd-backup: Preview a mirror export (writes nothing); drop --dry-run to run it
diagnostics.cmd-check: Audit storage and index, read-only (run it bare and read the exit code; --folder <space-dir> audits one claimed folder)
diagnostics.cmd-logs: The only log surface: the daemon log (add --json, or -i <instance>)
diagnostics.cmd-perm: Re-run the guest permission matrix alone
diagnostics.cmd-record: Run the self-check and record it — the source of the summary above; --help lists the checks and the record shape
diagnostics.cmd-repair: Rebuild one folder's ledger from disk
diagnostics.cmd-worker: Keep draining pending chain intents (long-running); run drains once
diagnostics.desc: Is this node healthy right now? The verdict of the last recorded self-check, when it ran, and every check one row at a time. This page executes nothing: it only visualises the recorded result and offers commands you copy and run yourself. Level-3 detail — commands, storage, logs, backup, permissions, background work, troubleshooting — is folded into the Advanced tab.
diagnostics.faq: A save looked accepted but the record is unchanged: the toast is not evidence — read the record back with arc afs exec /blocklets/arcblog/.actions/read --args '{"path":"<afs path>"}' --json (arc-contracts §29.4). A write was refused: conditional, not absolute — it depends on the record's origin, the write mode and the daemon process (§29.2); probe before deleting, because delete + recreate loses createdAt. A record disappeared from a filtered list: filter / serverFilters push a query to the index and an edit leaves its index entry stale (§15) — re-check through arc afs exec /blocklets/arcblog/.actions/list --args '{"path":"<dir>"}' --json. ?page=<id> silently lands on the public home: that id is not a registered page — the authoritative page set is the sidebar model, guarded in the fast tier (npm test). A read is denied for a signed-in session: the record's directory prefix decides (blocklet.yaml replicated.readRole / minRole, §13); there is no third role to grant. Storage keeps growing: audit read-only first, then rebuild one folder's ledger (both commands above); dev-instance test residue is swept by arcblog-clean.mjs, dry-run by default. A publish never reached the public site: record a self-check (command above) and read the space-layout / resources rows; Node registry state lives on ?page=registry.
diagnostics.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to see this instance's self-check results.
diagnostics.list-desc: One record per check, live-subscribed; the row count is whatever the last run recorded — this page hard-codes no number. severity and ok are shown as text, so a state never depends on colour alone.
diagnostics.sum-empty: No self-check snapshot yet — 尚未运行: nothing has been recorded here, so this card shows no verdict and no invented time. Empty is not the same as “all checks passed”. Run the record command on the Advanced tab first.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
factory.actions-desc: One click queues the intent; the node's chain worker signs it (the key never reaches the browser) and the queue below updates live.
factory.advanced-note: Addresses and transaction hashes read from node/factories.json; the public key is bound into the on-chain NFT template, and no key material is mirrored here. Whether a value is chain truth is decided PER NODE, never from the file header — see the attribution card.
factory.confirm-acquire-msg: The factory mints one Studio node NFT to this node's owner wallet, on chain, immediately.
factory.confirm-claim-msg: The NFT returns to the owner wallet and the stake closes.
factory.confirm-revoke-msg: Assets leave the stake and a waiting period starts before the final claim.
factory.confirm-stake-msg: The NFT locks into the factory stake and the role becomes staked.
factory.desc: The on-chain identity of this node: the SVG card it renders, the factories that mint it, and one-click buy / stake / revoke / claim.
factory.docs: Runbook and worker command: see the Diagnostics page.
factory.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view the node NFT and operate it.
factory.intent-queued: Intent queued — watch the queue below.
factory.projection: Read from the public projection node/factories.json; the authoritative records stay admin-only, and no key material is mirrored. Every state line (chain / node / card / transaction / status) is precomputed by the CLI and printed here verbatim, so each printed line is standing copy that must hold in every state. An empty state line means the projection has not been written yet — run the regeneration command above.
factory.queue-admin: The queue lives in config/ (admin-only): only the blocklet owner can queue or watch chain operations.
factory.queue-clear-msg: Removes the record from the queue. The chain transaction is unaffected.
factory.queue-standing-note: Every queued chain intent appears in the list above, oldest first: a row is written the moment a button is clicked, so an empty list simply means nothing has been queued on this node yet.
factory.render-timing: First-load note: on this platform the projection is bound AFTER the first render, so on a cold visit every field below can read the empty placeholder — that means "not bound yet / unavailable", never "the record is empty". Expand the advanced details or reload once to bind it (measured 2026-09-28: no channel recovers on its own).
factory.status-note: pending = waiting for the worker · applied = signed on chain · rejected = refused, nothing changed
factory.title: Node NFT
factory.truth-note: Each node records the adapter that produced its facts, in three states — mock (simulation, never chain truth) · ocap (real chain, verifiable) · unknown (nothing was ever recorded). The header adapter describes the factory config only, so it must never decide whether a node is chain truth — judge per node.
factory.truth-title: Is it really on chain? (per node)
factory.worker-hint: Queued actions are signed by this node's chain worker; the browser never holds the key.
feeds.desc: Subscription and index surfaces generated from published content.
feeds.feeds-agent: Agent access (llms.txt / MCP) is declared by the runtime.
feeds.feeds-desc: The RSS feed at /p/rss.xml is produced by the deploy pipeline: every deploy regenerates it and then checks that it answers. A bare build removes it, so deploy before you ship — ops manual step O8 has the details. The agent surfaces (/p/llms.txt, MCP) come from the runtime and need nothing.

general.basics-desc: Site-level values. They live in this blocklet's own config collection and are read by the RSS generator.
general.basics-error: Not saved — the write was refused and nothing changed. Check that a value is chosen (or filled in) and that the runtime allows the write; the console shows the platform error.
general.basics-guard: Each field offers only its own record's allowed values, so an out-of-options value cannot be submitted, and a field must be chosen (or filled) explicitly before Save. If an edit is refused nothing changes — the stored-records list below is the source of truth.
general.desc: Instance-level General settings — site name, language, timezone and the three Instance switches. These values are stored in this blocklet's own config collection and apply to the whole node.
general.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage this instance's General settings.
general.init-confirm-msg: Creates any missing record with its documented default; existing records are left untouched.
general.init-desc: Creates only the records that are missing, with their documented default; an existing record is never overwritten. They are ordinary records afterwards — both this page and the operator CLI can update them.
general.language-hint: Value of the RSS <language> element of the generated feed.
general.records-desc: What is actually stored. This list is the source of truth: if an edit above is refused, the value here does not change.
general.roles-cmd-init: Change the address / network from the CLI (the only path)
general.roles-config-desc: Collection address, network and assetType are record values (admin-only). This page only displays them; the commands below are the only way to change them.
general.roles-desc: This card shows the engine's own role state: the five lifecycle words and every derived value come from the role engine and its CLI, never from a second vocabulary typed into a page. The externalized config is read-only here, and changing an address or a network is an operator step only.
general.roles-factory-desc: These four actions live on the Node NFT page and are not duplicated here: each one queues an intent there and the node's chain worker signs it. This card only links there, so the purchase-to-stake guide stays inside the console.
general.roles-honesty: Honesty note: a leftover assetId in a record does NOT mean an asset is owned — ownership is derived from the lifecycle state. And this re-derivation is NOT a chain verification: no value on this card is chain truth.
general.roles-no-input: There is deliberately no address or network input on this page. A value shown as unbound means not bound yet / unavailable, never that the record is empty.
general.roles-source-note: Authoritative source for every value is the status command above; this card renders a projection, and the CLI wins when the two disagree.
general.roles-states: Lifecycle: none → acquired → staked → revoking → claimable. The page repeats these five words verbatim so a drift is visible; revoking derives to claimable at read time once the waiting period has passed — the record itself is not rewritten.
general.roles-states-note: Every state here is operator-declared: setting staked does NOT activate a role. Until a verifier is wired, every chain role stays inactive and its capabilities stay withheld (fail closed).
general.roles-status-desc: Derived by the CLI, never typed here. The reason string is shown verbatim: this console cannot translate a runtime value, and a paraphrase would hide the real cause.
general.roles-verify-confirm-msg: Writes one intent record only; the snapshot changes when the worker runs. Nothing is verified on chain.
general.roles-verify-desc: The button queues ONE intent record (admin-only, the same config collection as the policy queue — zero permission change). It runs nothing itself and never touches the role config. The node's worker consumes it:
general.roles-verify-error: Not queued — the write was refused and nothing changed.
general.roles-verify-kind: What the worker does: a read-only re-derivation of every role status from the existing records, plus a consistency report between the config and the public projection. It never flips the verification flag and signs nothing.
general.roles-verify-queue: One pending record is written; read it back — a toast is not evidence.
general.roles-verify-title: Re-verify — the real path (no fake button)
general.site-name-hint: Channel title of the generated RSS feed. It does not rename the blocklet or the console brand.
general.sw-agent-consumer: Consumed by the Agent Access CLI: when off, tool runs are refused and the switch is reported as disabled (fail closed). Takes effect on the next CLI run.
general.sw-agent-impact: Impact: every Agent Access tool call on this node. It does not affect the read-only public web surface.
general.sw-comments-consumer: No consumer yet — ArcBlog has no comment feature, so this switch is recorded only. It is not a fake control: the page says so, and the record can be read from the CLI.
general.sw-rss-consumer: Consumed by the RSS generator: when off, the feed keeps its channel but carries no items. Takes effect on the next generation.
general.sw-rss-impact: Impact: the public RSS feed (and therefore every subscriber). It does not remove published posts.
general.switches-desc: Instance-level master switches. Every switch states its impact and whether anything actually consumes it.
general.timezone-hint: IANA timezone used for the <pubDate>/<lastBuildDate> UTC offset of the generated feed.
general.title: Settings

media.adv-cmds: Media commands — copy this line, then pick one verb and fill in the id / AFS path
media.cmd-refs: Show where one asset is used (read-only information)
media.desc: Upload an asset, read this node's upload index, and reach the CLI commands that compute references and clean up (Advanced tab).

media.index-note: Each row is one record of this upload index: title, MIME type, byte size, indexed time, plus two copy buttons — the asset's AFS path and the refs command for that id. The record carries no public URL, so none is shown, and the index itself is maintained by the CLI, never by this page.
media.limits-join: Platform limits, stated instead of hidden: a page cannot join collections, so reference data (refs and the unreferenced list) is computed only by the CLI; the media collection is admin-only because a record exposes its upload path; there is no list/grid switch; and no record stores a public URL.
media.media-standing-note: The list above renders every record of this upload index. An empty list only means no asset has been indexed on this node yet — index one with the CLI command in the Advanced tab. This is a standing note, never a claim about the rows above.
media.orphans-order: Always run refs --id <id> first: it shows where the asset is used before you clean anything up.
media.orphans-record-only: remove deletes the index record only — it never deletes the binary file.
media.orphans-refuse: remove is refused while the asset is still referenced (exit 1, code CONFLICT): resolve the references first, or pass --force to override.
media.refs-note: refs prints the count plus each referring record (kind + slug + path) from posts / drafts / pages / page-drafts / heroes.
media.title: Media
media.upload-desc: Pick or drop a file. afs-dropzone is the platform's only upload primitive and is declared without props on purpose: this platform exposes no prop metadata for it (arc dsl schema), so no prop is invented.
media.upload-note: Measured 2026-09-27 on this instance: dropping a file fails with "Upload failed: targetDir must be a non-empty string" — the prop-less form is this repo's existing convention, so no prop is invented here. Even a successful upload would not create an index record: the binary lands in your own DID space, so the index stays CLI-maintained — the command is in the Advanced tab.
operations.desc: Live state of this node: health, discovery, media and agent grants.
operations.discovery-empty: How to publish it: run the command below (the page cannot publish it itself).

operations.render-timing: First-load note: the health and discovery projections are read straight from their record files, so they are here on the first load — no reload needed. A field rendered as — means the record does not carry that field, not that the node is unhealthy.

page-view.title: Page
pages.act-delete-msg: Pages have no soft delete — this removes the record.
pages.act-offline-msg: Queues ONE "Take offline" intent under config/page-intents/ — this page writes nothing to your records. This node's worker performs the move (reads the page, merges it into the private drafts area, then removes the public copy). Read the intent record back — a toast is not evidence.
pages.act-publish-msg: Queues ONE "Bring online" intent under config/page-intents/ — this page writes nothing to your records. This node's worker writes the public copy and removes the offline copy; an older public copy (written by the old CLI or by root authority) is replaced too, because the worker writes with this node's own authority — the very write the platform refuses when a page asks for it.
pages.created-ok: Page created offline. Bring it online when ready.
pages.desc: Standalone pages such as About. Two states only — online and offline; no post lifecycle, no RSS.
pages.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage standalone pages.
pages.list-empty: No pages yet. Create your first page above.
pages.offline-hint: Offline pages are admin-only. "Bring online" only queues an intent; the local worker performs the move. The list below the two page lists is that queue, read straight from AFS: action · status · message.
pages.offline-ok: Intent queued — read config/page-intents to confirm; the local worker takes the page offline.
pages.online-hint: Online pages are public at /pages/<slug>; they stay out of RSS. 「Take offline」 only queues an intent under config/page-intents/ — the local worker completes the move. 「Remove public copy」 is a different, immediate action: it hard-deletes the public record (pages have no soft delete).
pages.published-ok: Intent queued — read config/page-intents to confirm; the local worker brings the page online.
pages.title: Pages
posts.admin-archive-msg: Archive this post? Writes an archived copy into the private drafts area. The public post stays online until you remove it from public.
posts.admin-delete-msg: Soft-delete this record? It stays in the private area with status deleted and can be published again later.
posts.admin-publish-msg: Publish a copy of this draft? The draft stays in the private area and a public copy goes live — this page copies, it does not move.
posts.admin-unpublish-msg: Remove this post from public? Deletes the public record. Archive first if you want to keep a private copy.
posts.desc: Every story, by state. Publishing or archiving here COPIES the record and keeps both versions.
posts.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage drafts, published stories and archived records.
posts.title: Your studio
preview.notice: Draft preview — this record is not public.
preview.preview-delete-msg: The record stays in the archive with status deleted (soft delete).
preview.published-hint: Published. The draft copy is still in studio drafts — remove it when done.
preview.title: Preview
reader.title: Article
saved.add-note: A page write stores exactly the three fields below — a real record under the reader's own DID Space user scope, so a refresh reads it back from AFS rather than from a cache.
saved.cmd-where: Show both storage paths for a DID
saved.desc: A private reading list. Every record lives in the signed-in reader's own user scope (/user/arcblog/bookmarks/<slug>.json), which the platform only materialises for that caller — no other visitor and no other signed-in DID resolves the same list.
saved.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to keep a private reading list.
saved.gov-desc: This page lists and adds; it deliberately does not delete. Measured (REQ-028): an AUP page validates ALL of its inputs on ANY action submit, so one empty required field blocks every other action on the page — a page-side delete would be hostage to the add form below. Removal is therefore the CLI's job, exactly as on the other console pages.
saved.list-desc: One row per record under /user/arcblog/bookmarks/ in this session's own user scope. The path is caller-scoped, not a shared directory: the same URL resolves to a different list for a different DID, and a signed-out visitor has no /user view at all.
saved.list-empty: Nothing saved yet. An empty list means no record exists in this reader's user scope — the form below writes the first one.
saved.slug-hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, exactly as it appears in /posts/<slug>. The CLI enforces the same rule.
saved.title: Reading list
saved.where-note: Storage: this reading list lives in YOUR DID Space user scope, one copy per reader — the blocklet declares no permission for it, and nothing is kept platform-side.
seo.desc: Site distribution defaults this page owns. Node identity (name / description / OG image / endpoint) is read-only here: it lives in node/profile.json and only the CLI writes it (one writer per field).
seo.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage site-level SEO.
seo.profile-empty: If the fields below are empty, either no record exists yet or this page has not bound it yet — records are bound after the first load, so reload once.
seo.title: SEO
tags.clear-msg: Removes the record from the queue. Posts it already rewrote are unaffected.
tags.confirm-msg: Every post referencing the source tag is rewritten in place (version + content hash), on both the published and the draft side. The console queues it; the node's worker applies it.
tags.desc: Tags are free-form words on posts — there is no tag registry. Rename or merge to converge spelling variants.
tags.empty-body: A tag appears here as soon as a post carries one: add tags while writing, then press Refresh projection — the worker rebuilds this list from the posts. There is no tag registry.
tags.enqueue-failed: Could not queue the intent — nothing was written. Sign in as the blocklet owner and try again.
tags.f-from-hint: Pick an existing tag from the list on the right.
tags.f-hint: Stored form is lowercase with underscores; spaces, capitals and hyphens are normalized when the worker executes.
tags.f-unknown-hint: A tag that does not exist yet cannot be renamed — the worker records it as noop and writes nothing. Check the list on the right first.
tags.form-desc: A target that does not exist yet renames the tag; an existing target merges into it. Either way every referencing post is rewritten.
tags.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage the site.
tags.queue-desc: The console cannot rewrite posts itself: submitting only queues an intent, and this node's worker applies it. Nothing is rewritten until the worker runs.
tags.queue-legend: pending = waiting for the worker · applied = posts rewritten · noop = no article referenced the source tag, nothing written · rejected = refused, no post touched
tags.queued: Intent queued — the local worker applies it.
tags.refresh-hint: Counts and the timestamp come from a derived projection: Refresh queues a rebuild, and this node's worker regenerates it from the posts.
tags.title: Tags
general.roles-claimable-note: Waiting period: the raw value is shown above when the record carries one; this console deliberately renders no countdown, and an empty value must not read as just now.
general.roles-reason-note: How to read these rows: the label is this console's field name and the value is the role engine's own text, verbatim. Engine vocabulary: granted = the capability is granted; withheld = it is withheld (fail closed); yes / no = the boolean the engine derived; (none) = nothing is withheld (not a missing value). A granted role has nothing withheld — for the basic role, reason explains why the capability is implicit, not why it is withheld.
general.roles-two-stage-note: Reading the dashes: a dash means the record carries no such value, or the binding has not resolved yet — on a freshly opened tab the rows can all read as dashes until a reload. A dash never means there are no roles.
pages.queue-legend: pending = queued, not run yet · applied = the worker ran it · rejected = refused, zero change · noop = already in that state
pages.queue-empty-note: Empty state: when a list has no records this platform prints its own hard-coded English empty-list text, so this page cannot localize it. This note is standing and does not claim that any list is empty; the authority for the queue is the CLI command above.
compose-edit.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to edit this draft; save it back to the private drafts or publish it.
registry.check-chain-value: Chain explorer / general SDK: list stakes where receiver = the factory address (the public projection is on ?page=factory, record node/factories.json)
registry.check-desc: This page renders the projection node/registry.json; verify it against the chain itself — list stakes where receiver = the factory address with a chain explorer or a general SDK, and never trust a number this page cannot source.
registry.desc: Which nodes are staked to this node's studio factory — the on-chain registry view. The page reads the public projection node/registry.json, which the CLI writes from the chain query (listStakes, probes P-1/P-2 verified 2026-10-01); it carries public fields only, never key material.
registry.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view the registry status.
registry.probe-p1-value: Verified (2026-10-01, mock adapter): returned count = staked count, unstaked nodes absent, cursor pagination continues.
registry.title: Node registry
registry.pending-note: This page renders only what the projection node/registry.json says. The state line below is computed by the CLI (the AUP expression layer cannot compare or concatenate, so the page only prints the string): it distinguishes not-yet-generated / a sourced empty state / the node list, and it states the remedy for the first and second. A projection with no live node is NOT an assertion about the whole chain — it means this factory has no live stake row (dead rows, `assets` empty next to a non-empty `revokedAssets`, are excluded), so the count is live nodes, not raw stake rows.
registry.probe-p2-value: Verified (2026-10-01, ocap adapter on beta): the minimal query shape addressFilter.receiver + paging.{size,cursor} is accepted and the cursor paginates.
registry.status-wired: Wired end to end: the adapters enumerate the chain registry (listStakes — P-1 mock / P-2 ocap, both verified 2026-10-01), the CLI's registry refresh writes the projection, and this page renders it. The chain remains the source of truth — a refresh re-reads it.
registry.reach-labels: Four reachability states (PRD-NET-03): reachable / stale / never / offline — fixed names, never renamed.
agents.registry-source: on-chain registry projection (node/registry.json + one record per node) — the operator's registry refresh writes it; run that before reading
agents.registry-content: get_studio --content then reads that node's public surface over its staked endpoint (read-only)
compose-edit.runtime-note: The editor binds the draft record after the first load. If the fields stay empty, reload once — or open the studio and pick an existing draft.
page-view.runtime-note: The page below is read from the record bound to this address, so it is here on the first load — no reload needed. If the body area is empty, the record does not exist (or this session may not read it).
preview.runtime-note: The draft below is read from the record bound to this address, so it is here on the first load — no reload needed. If the body area is empty, the draft does not exist (or this session may not read it).
reader.runtime-note: The article below is read from the record bound to this address, so it is here on the first load — no reload needed. If the body area is empty, the record does not exist (or this session may not read it).
agents.summaries-note: Aggregated summaries: the read-only projections under node/summaries/ written by the operator CLI below (an empty list means none has been built yet — this page neither builds nor scores one). Every figure a row shows is that record's own totalNote/stateNote; this page must not recompute a total (B5).
factory.registry-link-value: This page is the NFT lifecycle record. Whether the node counts as a live registry entry is a separate projection — open the Registry page, or run the command on the right.
preview.write-note: Publish / delete need the record in the session binding, which the platform only attaches after the first render — reload once before using them.
factory.dropped-label: Stale role records dropped (computed by the CLI)
dashboard.anomalies-desc: One entry per detected anomaly class. No row means the standing line below is the verdict — it is what the checker itself reported, and when.
seo.identity-cli: Change it with the copyable command below (this page cannot write the node profile).
posts.empty-hint: An empty tab means that state holds no record yet — write one with New post.
dashboard.overview-desc: Counts measured by the operator CLI and printed here verbatim; the line under them states when — this page invents no number.
wrapper.admin-notice: Signed in, but this console needs a Blocklet admin — the lists here are admin-only.
